newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks dip as new rules spur panic selling.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks dip as new rules spur panic selling.

text.p: Dhaka stocks dipped 6.39 percent, halting a lingering rally, after news that Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) is reducing the range of price fluctuation to five percent from 10 percent of the previous rates, brokers said.
The DSE benchmark index fell 233.20 points or 6.39 percent at 3,415.54. Turnover was 308.8 million taka. Of 93 traded issues, 77 lost, 15 gained and one stock was unchanged.

"The regulators are in fact imposing correction. Investors got panicked by further limiting the price movement range," said broker Moshtaque Ahmed. BD Lamps shed 1,160 to 10,433 and Bangladesh Tobacco Co lost 47 to 415.
